    Rules & card actions

    Start & win

    Each player chooses one distributor to start active, then receives three cards in hand and no resources. Reach 12 active businesses to win. A player with no active distributors loses immediately, even if they still control legitimate businesses. Operators do not count as businesses.

    Income & crews

    Collect income at the start of each turn. Each active distributor produces one resource of its color. Each complete three-person crew grants the unique bonus shown on its crew seal. Legit businesses and operators produce nothing.

    Activate or cash

    Pay a card’s activation cost to put it in play. A distributor or operator costs one of its color. A legit business costs one matching resource plus one of any color. Cash an unactivated card for one resource of its color; a legit card can be cashed for any color. Cashed cards are discarded.

    Business capacity

    You have room for three distributors, plus three more for each active legit business. You may possess up to three legit businesses total, counting active cards and cards in your hand. If you draw a fourth, immediately cash any inactive legit business, including the one just drawn. Active legit businesses count toward victory and are immune to all operators.

    Operators

    Each player may have at most two active operators. With Club Circuit, an operator may affect up to two targets when you can pay each target cost. Additional operators can stay in hand. Using an operator frees a slot. Pay activation once, then pay to use the ability. Hitman: pay the target’s cost to discard one distributor. Ruffian: pay one of a chosen target’s color to return every active member of that crew to the rival’s hand. Fixer: pay twice the target’s cost to take one distributor. The operator is discarded after use.

    Draw & trade

    Your first draw each turn costs one resource of any color, the second costs two, the third costs three, and so on. The price resets each turn. Trade four resources of one color for one of another, or two for one with Hill Country. Arts District allows one distributor trade per turn after paying the costs of both the target and the gift.

    Hand & resource limits

    Hold up to seven cards and ten resources, or twelve resources with Night Shift. Activate or cash before drawing into a full hand. Choose which excess resources to discard after income. Forced returns beyond seven cards are discarded. A distributor acquired with no open slot waits in hand until you can pay to activate it.

    The deck

    The base game has 24 distributors in eight crews, six legit businesses and six operators. When the draw pile runs out, shuffle the discard pile back in. The rival follows the same rules.
